name: Nebraska

agency.name: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE)

localAgencies.name: Lincoln-Lancaster County Health Department
localAgencies.notes: Issues construction and operating permits (per EPA's CAA Permitting in Nebraska page). DWEE general permits are not available for new locations in Lancaster County.

localAgencies.name: Omaha Public Works Department, Air Quality Control Division
localAgencies.notes: Issues construction and operating permits (per EPA). DWEE general permits are not available for new locations in the City of Omaha.

overview: Nebraska's air program (formerly the Nebraska Department of Environment and Energy, NDEE; now the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, DWEE) issues state construction permits (Title 129, Chapter 3), federal PSD/NSR construction permits (Chapter 4), general construction and operating permits (Chapter 7), and Class I (Title V) and Class II (state minor) operating permits (Chapter 6). DWEE states Nebraska is in attainment for all ambient air quality standards. Lincoln-Lancaster County and Omaha run local programs; EPA Region 7 permits in Indian country.

permitTypes.name: State Construction Permit
permitTypes.description: Required before constructing, reconstructing, or modifying a source where potential emissions increase above the listed thresholds. All incinerators need a construction permit regardless of emissions. DWEE cites typical review of four to six months plus a 30-day public comment period, and a fee tiered by potential emissions.
permitTypes.quote: 15 tons per year (tpy) of PM10 (Particulate Matter 10 microns in diameter or smaller), 10 tons tpy of PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5 microns in diameter or smaller), 40 tpy of SO2 (Sulfur dioxide) or SO3 (Sulfur trioxide) or any combination thereof, 40 tpy of oxides of nitrogen (calculated as NO2), 40 tpy VOC (Volatile Organic Compounds), 100 tpy CO (Carbon Monoxide), 0.6 tpy Lead, or 2.5 tpy of any single HAP (Hazardous Air Pollutant) or 10 tpy of all HAPs combined. In addition, all incinerators, regardless of emissions, must have a construction permit.

permitTypes.name: Air General Permits (construction and operating)
permitTypes.description: Online general permits for: aggregate processing plants; drum mix and batch mix hot mix asphalt plants; truck mix concrete plants (controlled and uncontrolled loadout); diesel emergency engines (two versions); controlled incinerators (construction) and incinerator operating permit; and surface coating. Not available for new locations in Lancaster County, the City of Omaha, or tribal lands.

permitTypes.name: Federal Construction Permit (PSD)
permitTypes.description: Applies when a source's potential emissions reach the PSD major source level for its category and the project's net emissions increase meets significance levels.
permitTypes.thresholds: Major source: at least 100 tpy for one of 26 listed source categories or 250 tpy for other sources. Significant net increases listed by DWEE include PM 25 tpy, PM10 15 tpy, SO2/SO3 40 tpy, NOx 40 tpy, VOC 40 tpy, CO 100 tpy, lead 0.6 tpy (restated).

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: Applies to major sources in nonattainment areas. DWEE's page states Nebraska is currently in attainment for all ambient air quality standards.

permitTypes.name: Class I (Title V) Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Major source operating permit. Application forms are due within 12 months after emissions units begin operation or become subject to the requirement, whichever is earlier.
permitTypes.quote: 100 tons per year (tpy) of any criteria air pollutant* excluding lead; 10 tpy of any single hazardous air pollutant (HAP) or 25 tpy of a combination of HAPs; or 5 tpy of lead.

permitTypes.name: Class II (minor source) Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: State operating permit for synthetic minor sources (potential emissions above Class I levels, limited by federally enforceable conditions) and natural minor sources (potential below Class I levels but actual emissions above half of Class I levels). Incinerators need an operating permit regardless of emissions.
permitTypes.quote: 50 tpy of criteria pollutant except lead; 5 tpy of any single hazardous air pollutant (HAP) or 12.5 tons per year of a combination of HAPs; or 2.5 tpy of lead.

permitTypes.name: Low Emitter
permitTypes.description: A source with potential emissions above Class I levels but actual emissions below Class II levels may not need an operating permit. Submit the Low Emitter Worksheet for DWEE approval (at least one full year of operating data required) and keep records showing actual emissions stay below Class II levels.

oilAndGas.summary: DWEE's air permitting and general permit pages list no oil and gas specific air permit or registration. Oil and gas facilities follow the general construction and operating permit thresholds above, plus applicable federal NSPS (OOOO/OOOOa/OOOOb) and NESHAP (HH) requirements.

Construction fee tiers per 16-022: $250 if under 50 tpy, $1,500 for 50 to under 100 tpy, $3,000 for 100 tpy or more (single pollutant); general construction permit $250 for new sources.
